02 / MISSION GUARDRAILS

Three golden rules

These are simple learning guardrails, not universal prescriptions. The goal is to make concentration visible and decisions deliberate.

CONCENTRATION CHECK≤20%

Cap a sector bet

Use 20% as a personal warning line for any extra sector allocation. A broad index can itself exceed that level as market values change; the rule is about avoiding accidental overconfidence in your own tilts.

BUILD THE COREVOO

Start broad

A low-cost S&P 500 ETF such as VOO owns companies across all 11 sectors. One purchase gives you a diversified U.S. large-company foundation.

BEFORE YOU OVERWEIGHTKNOW

Understand the cargo

Read the fund objective, holdings, fees, and risks. A sector ETF is not “more diversified” just because it holds many stocks; those companies may share the same economic risks.

04 / FLIGHT MANUAL

Wisdom for the long trip

Passive investing is simple, but not effortless. The difficult part is usually behavior: staying patient, thinking clearly, and resisting unnecessary moves.

WARREN BUFFETT · PATIENCE
“The stock market is designed to transfer money from the Active to the Patient.”
A widely cited Buffett principle
01
Keep costs lowEvery fee is fuel that cannot keep compounding for you.
02
Think in decadesRetirement investing is a long mission, not a daily scoreboard.
03
Ignore the cockpit noiseNews can be urgent without being useful to your plan.
CHARLIE MUNGER · CLEAR THINKING
Invert, diversify, and avoid the mistakes that can end the mission.
↺
InversionAsk “What could make this fail?” Avoiding ruin comes before maximizing return.
×
Lollapalooza effectSeveral biases can combine and amplify one another. Excitement, social proof, and recent gains can make a risky bet feel obvious.
⌛
Opportunity costEvery dollar sent to one idea is a dollar not compounding somewhere else.
Final transmission: The smartest mission usually starts broad, keeps a reserve, and adds complexity only for a reason.
05 / YOUR LAUNCH PLAN

Simple first. Smarter over time.

For a beginner learning the system, the cleanest educational starting point is a broad U.S. stock-market core. International stocks and bonds can come later as goals, time horizon, and risk capacity become clearer.

1
Begin with the coreLearn with a 100% VOO model before adding complexity. This is a teaching sequence, not a personal recommendation.
2
Build an emergency reserveLong-term investments should not be the money you need for near-term surprises.
3
Expand with purposeStudy international diversification and bonds; add them only when you understand the role each plays.
